title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented UNI customs, including living campus rituals and clearly labeled historical traditions.

cards.title: The Green Beanie Rule
cards.subtitle: Historical Iowa State Teachers College tradition
cards.notes: View the archive image and treat this as history: first-year men once wore green beanies during specified daytime hours.
cards.short_summary: A former first-year identifier, not a current student requirement.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI documents that first-year men at Iowa State Teachers College were required to wear green beanies from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; the university says current first-year students do not face these rules.

cards.title: The Green Armband Rule
cards.subtitle: Historical Iowa State Teachers College tradition
cards.notes: Use the archival account to understand this retired custom: first-year women once wore green armbands marking them as new.
cards.short_summary: A historic counterpart to the green-beanie custom.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI documents that first-year women at Iowa State Teachers College wore green armbands so others knew they were new to campus.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; not a current expectation.

cards.title: Watermelon on the First Day
cards.subtitle: Historical Orientation Week tradition
cards.notes: Look through the yearbook and newspaper images for this former opening-week gathering, traditionally held during fall Orientation Week.
cards.short_summary: A recurring early-1900s watermelon feed that connected students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI records date the watermelon feed or feast to the early 20th century and identify Orientation Week as its traditional timing.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition that continued on and off through much of the 1900s.

cards.title: Spring at UNI, Literally
cards.subtitle: Historical 1971–1980 spring celebration
cards.notes: Explore the archived photos of SUNI Daze, a formal spring celebration with picnics, concerts, regatta races, and playful contests.
cards.short_summary: A 1970s spring festival whose name meant “Spring at UNI.”
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that SUNI Daze, meaning “Spring at UNI,” formally celebrated spring from 1971 through 1980.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; the documented formal celebration ran from 1971 to 1980.

cards.title: The Long-Running Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Historical 1943–2000 campus holiday ceremony
cards.notes: Read the campus history before visiting the former sites near Commons and Maucker Union; the ceremony moved locations over its run.
cards.short_summary: A holiday gathering that united campus members across generations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies the Tree Lighting Ceremony as a long-standing campus holiday tradition held from 1943 to 2000.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; it is documented as having ended in 2000.

cards.title: Learn the Six-Move “Interlude”
cards.subtitle: Panther Welcome and McLeod Center tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the six-movement dance at Panther Welcome or athletics events, where UNI says new students still learn and perform it.
cards.short_summary: A UNI-created synchronized dance born in 2010.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that new students still learn the “Interlude” during Panther Welcome and that it is often done at athletics events in the McLeod Center.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on Panther Welcome and athletics-event programming.

cards.title: Build a UNI Traditions Record
cards.subtitle: Alumni & Friends participation challenge
cards.notes: Document completed traditions with photos and follow the challenge guidance; 25 completions earn a pin and 45 earn a commencement medallion.
cards.short_summary: A continuing challenge that recognizes participation in UNI customs.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI says the Traditions Challenge continues as part of student experience and currently features 65 UNI traditions.
cards.access_notes: Review current challenge instructions and any event-specific requirements before participating.

cards.title: Ring In, Ring Out
cards.subtitle: Arrival, finals, and commencement tradition
cards.notes: Find the Sesquicentennial Bell to mark an arrival or graduation milestone; UNI also encourages rubbing it for good luck during finals.
cards.short_summary: A new bell ritual tied to the beginning and close of a UNI career.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that students are encouraged to ring the Sesquicentennial Bell when they arrive and around Commencement, and to rub it for finals luck.
cards.access_notes: UNI describes this as a new tradition introduced in the prior year.

cards.title: Meet Beneath the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Homecoming midnight Campanile tradition
cards.notes: If Homecoming programming includes campaniling, gather at the Campanile for the documented midnight ritual; respect event guidance and the space.
cards.short_summary: A revived Homecoming custom centered on UNI’s bell tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI Archives documents campaniling as kissing under the Campanile at midnight, revived for Homecoming in 1979 and part of Homecoming celebrations since.
cards.access_notes: The documented ritual is associated with Homecoming; participation is optional and event programming may vary.

cards.title: Start With Panther Welcome
cards.subtitle: Current UNI arrival tradition
cards.notes: Check the current welcome schedule when arriving on campus; UNI lists Panther Welcome among its recognized traditions and teaches the Interlude there.
cards.short_summary: A current welcome ritual that introduces new Panthers to campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies Panther Welcome among today’s recognized campus traditions and states that new students learn the “Interlude” during it.
cards.access_notes: Consult current university orientation communications for dates and participation details.
